notes: Scope: 166 claims in the theme; most are narrative, internal-protocol or archive-specific (Assembly Chorus, SPXI, RES, Glas function, Bead Count tiers) with no external analogue, and were not searched. Searched lines: cross-model and longitudinal convergence (857.F1, 803.B2), alignment and diversity (107.G1), recursive-training collapse and real-data thresholds (782.A7, 635.F1, 1573.F4), machine-text predictability (110.A1, 110.F2), code monoculture (199.A1, 199.A2, 199.F1), chat data (856.B1, 856.F1), academic discourse (476.A2, 476.A3, 1540.F3), mediation design (779.F4), diversity benchmarks (855.F1), hallucination regularity and seeding (1287.E1, 1287.E3, 21.B2), evaluator gaming and humanizers (741.B2, 1540.B1), entity tail (782.A5), adoption (124.B1), RAG self-retrieval (923.B2, 1088.B1), poetic jailbreaks (1205.F2, 1251.B1). Disconfirmations: B-collapse-W25 (Kosch et al., CHI writing: prose did not homogenize, vocabulary grew more varied) against 476.A2's academic-discourse component; it sits beside B-collapse-W22, W23 and W24, which support that component in biomedicine, natural science and Scopus-wide. B-collapse-W05 (Fortier, Chen & West, EMNLP 2026) locates output homogeneity in pretraining with alignment as amplifier, which tells against safety pressure as the origin named by 803.B2; it also bears on 107.G1, whose predicted direction (instruct below base) it leaves standing while contesting RLHF as the source, so it was not linked there; the main session may wish to add a 107.G1 link with that scope. On 855.F1: NoveltyBench (W29) predates the claim and is a benchmark of output diversity; the claim's sentence that no such benchmark exists in any deployed evaluation framework stands only on a narrow reading of 'deployed'. Recorded as method support; the operator may rule it a disconfirmation of that sentence. W-0003 (de Rooij & Biskjaer) may also bear on PRED-779.F4 as method in part: a reanalysis of existing AI-creativity studies with a moderator (task constraint); the claim's moderator is mediation design, so the fit is partial. It does not bear on 476.A3's population-level trajectory. Anticipations: most witnesses predate their claims (the collapse literature from 2023–2024, the alignment-diversity literature from 2023–2025). After-registration witnesses: W02 (857.F1, 803.B2), W05, W19 (199.A2), W25 (476.A2, 1540.F3), and W37's arXiv version. Evidence classes needing care: W37 is a company research post by Graphite's officers, with an arXiv version; W34 is news reporting a figure from an integrity-software founder whose method is not described; W20 is a vendor announcement. Quotes: WebFetch returns verbatim fragments of at most about 120 characters, so long abstracts are quoted in pieces; every quote was requested character for character from the fetched page. The summarizer's paraphrase was never used as a quote. Not resolved: PRED-782.A7 part (3), the critical α in 0.05–0.15, has threshold existence results (W12, W13) and no value in the claim's terms; Garg et al. (2509.22341) give an optimal ratio near 0.618 for linear interpolation, a different quantity, logged as excluded. PRED-199.A1's generational SSDI decline has no direct measurement in code; W03 and W02 show generational decline in text. PRED-107.G3 (human-rated slop and signed deviation): Shaib et al. relate slop to coherence and relevance and do not test deviation. Prose rule: two verbatim quotes (W23, W27) contain a phrase the prose rules bar outside quotation; they are left as found.
